Wroxton CE Primary School is a small, nurturing village school on the outskirts of North Banbury. We are proud to be part of the Oxford Diocesan Schools Trust, who support us in fulfilling our vision—where every child is encouraged to dream, empowered to aspire, and inspired to achieve their potential, fostering a community of lifelong learners.

This week Hedgehogs have been making the numbers 11 - 20 using lots of different manipulatives so they really understand what each written number represents. They have been doing lots of counting, as well as finding one more and one less.
Foxes love coming to school on time so they can enjoy our Early Morning Work- today was maths games. The children practiced their multiplication skills and four digit place value. They are super speedy!
House Points 2026/2027 Week 2 totals. Birch keep the top position. 1st Birch 538 2nd Oak 497 3rd Maple 453
Fabulous Foxes created their own toothpastes today: they followed a recipe, added optional elements such as colouring and flavoring and designed their toothpaste tube. Each toothpaste was assessed using the Bright Smile Company criteria: aroma, appearance, ability to remove plaque (marker pen) and ability to stay on the brush. Each team will receive their feedback on Monday.
This week in religion and world views, Badgers were thinking about 'what makes a good life'. We talked about what pleasure, peace and happiness mean and if they mean the same for everyone. We discussed this through different scenarios. The children were then asked to write down 9 things that connect them with a 'good life'. They ranked these in order from the most important at the top to the least important at the bottom. The different answers were very interesting!
Linked to our English text for this term 'The Naughty Bus' Year 2 went on a bus trip to Banbury and back. We walked to the bus stop and waited for the bus, we were very excited when a double decker bus arrived! We bought our return tickets and sat at the front at the top, this gave us a great view. We talked about what we saw on the way, identifying different vehicle types, different areas of town, why buses have numbers and discussing how a bus is different to travelling by car. Thank you to bus driver Mark who was very welcoming.

Badgers! What a fantastic start to the new school year! We have done some amazing safety learning this week, including '999 what's your emergency', fire safety and keeping safe within our community. We have been so impressed with how well our year 5 and 6 children have settled back into school. They have shown such maturity, enthusiasm and responsibility, and it has been wonderful to see them stepping confidently into their roles as our oldest pupils! Our Badgers are such important role models within our school community. The way they behave, the choices they make and the example they set have a real impact on our younger children. They help to shape the values and culture of our whole school and we are looking forward to seeing them grow, lead and inspire others throughout the year!
Hedgehogs have begun the school year by learning about road and bike safety. We have learnt to 'stop, look, listen, think' when crossing the road. We went out on the playground (in the rain!) and practised crossing the road while some children were on vehicles. We practised using a zebra and pelican crossing too. When learning about bike safety we ensured we had our helmets on, checked our brakes, tyres and bell.

PE and Sports Premium
Principles for the Funding
From September 2013, all primary schools across England have received a share of the Government's £150m pa Primary Physical Education and Sports Premium. The funding is ring-fenced and must be spent on improving the provision and quality of PE and sport in primary schools so that pupils develop healthy lifestyles.
PE at Wroxton
Physical Education (PE) is an integral part of the curriculum at Wroxtron. As well as providing high quality exercise, we believe PE boosts confidence in children and breaks down barriers, creates long-lasting memories, builds teamwork and helps to bring the children together, which creates a real sense of community. ​ Aims
To promote a healthy and active lifestyle.
Special Events
Throughout the year, we hold a number of PE focused events where we raise the profile of the subject.
We run charity sports events supporting a range of different charities. This year we will be raising money for a local charity close to many of our school community, The Katharine House Hospice, where we will be holding a Santa Fun Run on the field. Every child will donate £1 to take part as well as collecting sponsorship money to take on an exciting obstacle race. ​ Towards the end of the year, we hold our annual sports day which includes all children in the school winning points for their houses. It is always a very inclusive event that showcases the strong community feel we have at Wroxton with a focus given to our values as well as succeeding in the various events.
NOSSP Festivals and Tournaments
​At various times throughout the year, different children from across the school are chosen to participate in festivals and tournaments with children from other schools in Banbury. We aim to ensure that children have the opportunity to represent the school at a minimum of one event by the end of their key stage. These events are always very popular and children enjoy attending them and participating in healthy competition.

SEND and Inclusion
About our school
Wroxton Primary School is a mainstream school which provides for children with a wide range of special educational needs and disabilities, including those with:
​Our aim is to identify areas where children may be under achieving or having learning difficulties at an early stage. We identify those with additional needs using OCC guidance, and inform parents if we think children require additional support.
Where children are identified as needing additional learning or behavioural support, the school adheres to the SEND Code of Practice. We ensure that each child's needs are individually and appropriately catered for, and that any relevant outside agencies are involved in providing guidance and support.
We assess all children regularly and plan for their provision in class and any additional interventions in a smaller group. This is recorded in a Pupil Profile. For those on the SEND register, progress is reviewed and outcomes agreed three times in the school year with parents and children.
We aim to work closely with parents and children, respond to any concerns and celebrate achievements. In a small number of cases where there is still a lack of progress, perhaps where there are more complex needs and a range of external agencies the school may apply for an Education Health and Care Plan. Our Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Co-ordinator (SENDCo) is: Ms. Sara Bailey
Ms. Bailey can be contacted through the school office: Tel: 01295 730298 or by emailing: deputyhead@wroxtonprimary.co.uk
She holds the National Award in Special Educational Needs (Oxford Brookes University, July 2013).
The Governors and staff at Wroxton Primary School are committed to meeting the educational needs of all our pupils through the provision of challenging and exciting experiences.
We celebrate their diversities and differences by embracing an inclusive ethos throughout the school. We recognise that quality learning takes place when we motivate pupils, promote their self-esteem and develop the skills and aptitudes they require to enable them to make their way as lifelong learners.
The Governor with SEND responsibility is: Mrs Jane Maharry Mrs Jane Maharry can be contacted through the School Office Tel: 01295 730298 Email: office@wroxtonprimary.co.uk

Safeguarding Children in Banbury
We are proud to be members of SCiB and appreciate your help and support in promoting the good work of this Banbury initiative.
Please click the button to go to the SCiB website:
SCIB was set up (initiated by Thames Valley Police) to develop preventative education to help raise understanding and aim to address key issues faced by the communities of Banbury.
The three major issues that children are falling victim to in Banbury are Substance Abuse, Misuse of Online Materials and Child Exploitation (including sexual exploitation). The proposal from the SCIB team is that in each long term, 4 lessons will be planned and resourced to be delivered through PSHE sessions in school. It became apparent that some teachers felt they needed more information to build their confidence or knowledge around delivering the content (e.g. I hadn’t heard of Nitrous Oxide but this is a real issue in Banbury). As a result, we have teamed up with professionals who will deliver short and fact-filled sessions that staff can attend related to the content they are delivering. This is a model we will follow for all of the three strands.
The curriculum has been constructed around instilling protective behaviours for pupils to enable them to build the tools to keep themselves safe in unknown scenarios and then also include a ‘SCIB knowledge session‘ that addresses the strand. Children will be taught to understand their Early Warning Signs, Risk Assess and Take Action. The curriculum has taken objectives from the PSHE Association and links completely with expected coverage and so this can replace content of a similar nature or be used to enhance it.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wroxton Church of England Primary School - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
We recognise that all children are on a developmental Learning Journey which starts with the Foundation Stage Curriculum. We aim, through our KS1 and KS2 curriculum plans, to build on these secure links in learning and enable children to make natural and powerful connections between subjects and disciplines. This work starts in our Foundation Stage with ‘in the moment’ planning and extends through to Y6, by which time children can select the subject and knowledge they need to draw upon and within which they can work to further develop their skills and knowledge to enable them to make a successful transfer to secondary school.
Throughout our curriculum, we value and take every opportunity to develop children’s understanding of the world they live in and the opportunities life offers them. We do this within their community and environment and also by stretching our horizons to offer children experiences and exposure to venues, events and occasions which they may not otherwise have the opportunity to experience.
English is an essential tool for communication and we prioritise vocabulary acquisition throughout the school curriculum. Reading is a golden thread in our curriculum that supports and enables children to make sense of the world around them.
Religion and Worldviews
We understand the importance of enabling children to develop an understanding of different religions and worldviews. This understanding fosters empathy in children and encourages them to consider their own thoughts, feelings and viewpoints of the world they live in.
Through these subjects, we encourage children to become curious learners who think critically to help them develop solutions to complex problems.
Knowledge and Understanding of the World
These subjects help children to understand and get to know other people, the place where they live and about all aspects of the environment.
These subjects play a central role in shaping our sense of personal, social and cultural identity. They also support children to recognise and value the variety and vitality of culture locally, nationally and globally.
Health and Wellbeing
Learning in health and wellbeing ensures that children and young people develop the knowledge and understanding, skills, capabilities and attributes which they need for mental, emotional, social and physical wellbeing now and in the future.
Continuous Provision
From the very start of their Wroxton School journey, our children show us that play is our brain’s favourite way of learning, which is why it’s the centre of our EYFS and KS1 curriculum. We believe that continuous provision helps independent, inquisitive and motivated learners to flourish by meeting the language, social, emotional and physical needs of our children.
Continuous provision at Wroxton enables children from all backgrounds to have the same opportunities, providing a rich variety of practical experiences. Children are encouraged to take responsibility for extending and practising what they have been learning and complete challenges which are designed to foster and ignite their curiosity.
Children are taught to use life-long skills such as perseverance, problem solving and responsibility in their day-to-day routine and plan their own learning enquiries. The flexibility and ownership that children have of their learning means that opportunities can be easily adapted to meet the specific needs of each individual child – no matter what their starting point. ​
How is it planned and documented?
Our curriculum is designed annually in consultation with children and staff. Pupil voice is gathered through end-of-year surveys and discussions about projects. Children identify what they have enjoyed learning and what they would like to learn the following year, which is taken account of at the next stage of design.
Next, teams of teachers work in phases to plan the curriculum, taking account of previous learning (evaluations/coverage/monitoring). This stage takes place as a whole school planning event; utilising subject leader expertise, prior knowledge of curriculum, knowledge of cohorts and what the community has to offer. This planning stage results in the formation of a Curriculum overview.
Curriculum overviews
This document maps out the year and is archived to plot a cohort’s journey through school. These identify the subjects to be covered, the WOW, trips and visitors and EXPO opportunities for each project. These are monitored by the SLT in the first instance and then reviewed by hub teams to ensure coverage of subjects.
Long term plan
Once the curriculum overview has been agreed, it is used to create a long-term overview designed for parents and children, which is sent home and displayed on website.
Projects
The next stage of the planning process is to focus on the project.
Project planners
This document is subject-specific and identifies the objectives to be covered, the vocabulary to be taught, the questions that will asked and the intended outcomes for ability groups of children with each project.
The project planner is a working document and evaluations of the project influence next steps in terms of curriculum design and also projects planned for the year.
Medium term organiser
A breakdown of week by week coverage to plot the intended coverage.
How is our curriculum assessed?
Curriculum maps
This is a parent and child friendly document identifying the details of the subjects being covered in the topic – sent home and displayed on the website.
How is the curriculum monitored?
Pupil voice
Book scrutiny
Lesson observations
Wows!
These are designed to engage children with their learning. A wow day might be in the form of a trip or a visitor, a series of collaborative challenges or an aspect of the project to be taught later on. We want our children to be excited to come to school and have a passion for learning. These engaging days give the children a flavour of what is to come.
Trips and visitors
We use trips as a starting point for our learning so that the experiences children have during a trip add a layer onto learning. Trips are planned with learning objectives in mind, and we liaise with establishments to get the most out of the visit. Visitors are used to add expertise into our curriculum – with children being able to meet someone connected with the topic either through their job or interest.
Expos
This is a chance to share the learning that has taken place. Expos can be; a performance, a pop-up museum, children teaching others, a gallery of work, or an observed lesson. Some Expos are for parents, some are for the community and other classes within the school. The expos give children experience of presenting to an audience and a chance for our community to see learning outcomes.
Homework
We encourage children to read every night and develop number fluency. We send home English and maths tasks to support our learning in class; either as a pre-teach task or a consolidation task. Each week there is a homework task that is linked to the project learning for children in Years 1–6.
If you have any questions about our curriculum or would like to find out more, please contact: ​office.3004@wroxton.oxon.sch.uk or call 01295 730298

Badgers: Year 5 and Year 6
Squirrels are our youngest children at Wroxton Primary School, welcoming Reception and Year 1 pupils into our school community. They are curious, enthusiastic learners who enjoy exploring, discovering and developing new skills every day. Their teachers are Mrs Jennings and Mrs Orchard, and they are supported by Mrs Clayton and Mrs Woodcock.

All About Squirrels
Squirrels are an excitable bunch who love practical learning, learning through our play and teamwork. We care, we are helpful and we are inclusive – everyone matters and everyone belongs!
We have a very busy role-play area, a well-loved art workshop and an amazing construction area. We are also big fans of our outdoor classroom – water play and the sandpit are current favourites of ours!
Our Teachers
​Since graduating as a teacher in 1995, I have discovered my true passion is Early Years. When I'm not at school, I enjoy spending time with my teenage children and friends and like country walks and trips to the theatre and cinema.
I have taught in Kent, Buckinghamshire, Hertfordshire and Oxfordshire in Early Years, KS1 and KS2 classes. In my spare time, I enjoy spending time outside, visiting the seaside and reading.

Our approach to EYFS and Year 1
In Squirrels, we learn in a variety of different ways. Sometimes we have whole class input/carpet time. Sometimes we will be learning in small groups with an adult (both indoors and outdoors). Reception children often learn through our play, and our adults step in to ask important questions that help us to think and extend our play. We also have ‘Busy Time’ where we improve our skills in our enhanced provision. We can choose our area of learning and use the resources provided to consolidate previous learning.
Phonics
Phonics is taught daily in groups, working on a specific set of sounds according to the ability of the child. Each session has a distinct structure following Read Write Inc (RWI). Each week, the children take home new sound cards, Ditty sheets or a RWI book for them to re-read each night with an adult. This helps them develop fluency.

Books to support our learning
Our key books this term are stories featuring dragons. In 'The Knight and the Dragon' by Tomie DePaola a knight and a dragon prepare for battle but ultimately become friends and form a BBQ business together. In Emma Yarlett’s ‘Dragon Post’, a boy named Alex finds a dragon in his house. He writes a series of letters asking for help. The replies from the fire brigade, local butchers and so on, are included in the book. The story ends with a very special postcard for Alex. Additionally, our daily stories and reading enrichment activities will enable the class to encounter different familiar and project linked stories and non-fiction texts.
